title: Scheduler expansion admission
description: Objective: validate one sealed expansion proposal through landed graph/dependency/quality, scope/oracle/materialization evidence, conserved-budget/resource, and real fairness-capacity surfaces and return one all-or-none prepared admission. Hard dependencies: task-93b0314e09f248118e21f92699989468 and Fair scheduler production task-10cab3e5cdad4296bd7632bcda7b20f3 must be DONE with committed symbols. Deliverable: a dependency-free evidence validator plus admission composer with a closed EXPANSION code/layer vocabulary and exact preparation identity. NOT in scope: policy evaluation, approval, child activation, persistence, daemon composition, or importing @moe/core/@moe/runner. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-evidence.ts, expansion-evidence.js, expansion-admission.ts, expansion-admission.js, expansion-admission.test.ts. Production consumers: the core approval-binding child and task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: The evidence validator derives exact scope-disjointness, child oracle eligibility, input materializability, containment, completion closure, freshness, and source digests from closed immutable receipt shapes; missing, malformed, caller-positive, or UNKNOWN evidence never passes.

The admission entry point reuses admitGraph/checkExpansionLineage, conserved-budget reservation, all-resource reservation, and the landed real fairness capacity/opportunity verdict, enforcing exact limits 3/6/9 and returning one result for the complete proposal.

Any quality, scope, oracle, input, budget, resource, capacity, dependency, freshness, containment, or limit failure returns one frozen all-or-none refusal with exact expansion code and layer (or verbatim delegated code/layer) and no proposal/preparation/child authority.

Success returns one immutable identity binding proposal/revision, quality/dependency, scope/oracle/input, budget/resource reservations, fairness opportunity/cap revision, capacity snapshot, goal version, graph epoch, and source-fact digests; any byte change yields a different identity and re-admission.

Focused N/N+1, stale/race, hostile, precedence, replay, nonzero generated-case, zero-partial-child, and production mutation tests pass; the exact verification exits 0, production files stay below 400 lines, and no DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/cross-package import exists.
taskRails: If Fair scheduler production or any named symbol is absent/uncommitted, report blocked; never substitute caller-declared capacity or testkit fairness.
UNKNOWN evidence never counts as scope, oracle, input, capacity, budget, resource, quality, or dependency proof.
This pure kernel creates no child run, lease, effect, slot, allocation activation, or graph mutation.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED for the evidence validator (DoD 1). Create packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-admission.test.ts covering expansion-evidence first.

DoD 1 names seven derivations, each from CLOSED IMMUTABLE RECEIPT SHAPES: exact scope-disjointness, child oracle eligibility, input materializability, containment, completion closure, freshness, and source digests. Test each separately — they fail independently and collapsing them hides which one broke.

THE CENTRAL PROPERTY, and taskRail 2 states it outright: missing, malformed, CALLER-POSITIVE, or UNKNOWN evidence NEVER passes. The caller-positive case is the one to write first and the one this whole task exists to prevent — a caller asserting "scope is disjoint" must gain nothing. Prove it: hand the validator a receipt whose caller-declared verdict says eligible while the derived facts say otherwise, and assert refusal.

Every refusal pins the exact expansion code AND layer. Where the refusal is DELEGATED from a composed surface, DoD 3 requires the code/layer be passed through VERBATIM — so assert the delegated code, not a re-wrapped local one; re-coding a delegated refusal loses which layer actually refused.

Assert a generated sweep produced a NON-ZERO case count.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED for DoD 1. Test file created; suite red for the right reason: `Error: Cannot find module './expansion-evidence.js'`, 1 failed | 41 passed, 1047 tests still passing (baseline intact, so the red is mine and is the intended one).

THE CALLER-POSITIVE CASES ARE FIRST AND ARE THE STRUCTURAL ONES. Rather than testing "a caller verdict that contradicts the derived answer is refused", the design makes a caller verdict REFUSABLE ON SIGHT: `FORBIDDEN_VERDICT_KEYS` is a frozen exported list (scopeDisjoint, oracleEligible, inputsMaterialized, capacityAvailable, admissible, eligible) and any receipt carrying one is refused with the dedicated code EXPANSION_CALLER_DECLARED_VERDICT at layer EVIDENCE.

Three tests, and the third is the one that matters:
- `it.each(FORBIDDEN_VERDICT_KEYS)` sweeps every forbidden key at the top level.
- a verdict hidden inside a CHILD, not at the top — a top-level-only check would pass the sweep and fail this.
- *** a caller verdict that AGREES with the derived answer. *** This is the case a permissive implementation passes, because nothing it checks disagrees. Presenting a verdict at all is the defect, not presenting a wrong one. A "contradiction" test cannot express that.
Plus a guard that the sweep ran over a NON-EMPTY frozen key set — a sweep generating zero cases passes while testing nothing.

WHY A DEDICATED CODE RATHER THAN FOLDING INTO MALFORMED: the unknown-extra-key guard would also refuse these, so the test would stay green while the property migrated to a generic shape check. A distinct code keeps the assertion attached to its subject.

SEVEN DERIVATIONS, SEVEN INDEPENDENT TESTS, each perturbing exactly ONE field of a shared healthy receipt: scope overlap (SCOPE), containment (CONTAINMENT), oracle ineligible (ORACLE), input not materializable (INPUT), completion not closed (CONTAINMENT), stale receipt (FRESHNESS), source digest mismatch (SOURCE). Each asserts exact code AND exact layer.

A test asserts the HEALTHY receipt passes, which is what makes the other seven meaningful — without it, every perturbation test could be refusing for a shared unrelated reason.

AND A SET-COVERAGE GUARD over the seven: it runs all seven perturbations, collects the produced codes into a Set and asserts `size === 7`. Seven named tests read like seven covered derivations even when two trip the same guard; only the set comparison tells them apart. Same defect class the epic rail names for swept cases.

UNKNOWN IS A DISPOSITION, NOT A REFUSAL. The fairness contract this package already ships separates `disposition: "REFUSED" | "UNKNOWN"` — REFUSED means the value is wrong, UNKNOWN means an input needed to classify it was never supplied. I mirror that: an UNKNOWN materialization or completion yields disposition UNKNOWN with code EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN and a NON-NULL `missingInput` naming the exact path (`childScopes[0].inputs[0].materialization`). Collapsing the two would let a missing fact read as a refuted one, and taskRail 2 forbids UNKNOWN counting as proof of anything.

HOSTILE INPUTS: null/string/array/number all malformed; a missing required key yields EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_MISSING naming it; an unknown extra key is REFUSED rather than ignored (ignoring unknown keys is how a future caller verdict slips in under a name this version has never heard of); a `__proto__` payload parsed from JSON must not be consulted through the prototype chain; a non-hex source digest is malformed.

VOCABULARY COMPLETENESS: a test asserts `new Set(EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_ISSUE_CODES)` equals the exact set of 11 codes this file actually produces. A vocabulary entry no guard can emit is a claimed guard that does not exist; this makes adding an unreachable code a failing test rather than decoration.

Frozen-output tests included: the derived value is deeply frozen so a consumer cannot rewrite a verdict after the fact.

GREEN part 1. typecheck exit 0; suite 42 files / 1078 tests, 0 failed (baseline 41 / 1047, so +1 file and +31 tests). Both new production files well under target: expansion-evidence.ts 218, expansion-receipt.ts 209.

*** THE FILE HIT EXACTLY 400 LINES AND I SPLIT IT — 400 IS NOT "BELOW 400". *** As one module the validator measured 400 by `grep -c ''`. DoD 5 says production files stay BELOW 400 and the epic rail targets <=250, so 400 fails both readings. Step 3 pre-authorises the remedy ("split the receipt shapes out rather than overflowing"), so I split by RESPONSIBILITY rather than trimming comments to sneak under a bar:
  expansion-receipt.ts 209 — the closed receipt shape, the refusal vocabulary, and the readers
  expansion-evidence.ts 218 — the seven derivations and the order they run in
Both are needed to state a refusal, which is why they were one file; the package already splits this way (fairness-contract.ts beside its validators). Two extra owned paths (+ its LF .js bridge), 7 total, inside the 10-file cap.

A REAL BUG THE TYPECHECKER CAUGHT, worth recording because it fails silently in JS: `readOwnDataProperty` returns a DISCRIMINATED READ RESULT `{ok, present, value}`, not the value. I had used it as though it returned the value, so `isPlainArray(readOwnDataProperty(...))` was always false and TypeScript narrowed the else branch to `never` ("Property 'length' does not exist on type 'never'"). In plain JS this would have made every list read refuse as malformed — every derivation reachable, every test still red for the wrong reason. Fixed with a local `own()` that unwraps it once.

`own()` returns a SYMBOL, not undefined, for a key that is not a plain data property (a getter, or a throwing proxy trap). Two reasons: a getter can read differently on the second look, which is exactly the race a derived verdict must not be exposed to; and returning `undefined` would let a caller forge the same result by supplying a literal undefined. Every `typeof` check downstream rejects the symbol naturally.

THE CALLER-VERDICT GUARD RUNS BEFORE THE UNKNOWN-KEY GUARD, deliberately, and `checkKeys` does the two passes in that order. A verdict key IS also an unknown key, so a single pass would let the caller-verdict property be certified by a generic shape guard — and the day that guard is reorganised the property stops being tested with every assertion still green. Separate passes keep EXPANSION_CALLER_DECLARED_VERDICT attached to its own subject.

CONTAINMENT IS ANSWERED BEFORE DISJOINTNESS, and the order is part of the contract: a key outside the parent scope is not the parent's to hand out at all, so asking whether two children collide over it would answer a question that cannot arise. This makes a refusal deterministic for a given receipt rather than dependent on child order.

UNKNOWN CARRIES THE EXACT PATH. `disposition: "UNKNOWN"` with `missingInput: "childScopes[0].inputs[0].materialization"` — the test asserts that literal string, so an UNKNOWN that forgot to say what was missing fails. Mirrors the fairness contract's own REFUSED/UNKNOWN split rather than inventing a second spelling.

A MATERIALIZED input must carry a digest PRESENT IN the receipt's own sourceDigests. Otherwise the input names bytes that nothing ties to the facts this admission is about — materializable but unbound.

NOT YET DONE, and deliberately: this module does NOT import @moe/core. Step 3 suggests composing validExpansionProposalIdentity here, but the evidence validator is specified as DEPENDENCY-FREE (task description: "a dependency-free evidence validator plus admission composer") and every derivation is reachable from a plain object because of it. The sealed-proposal identity check belongs in the composer at step 5, where the @moe/core edge already is. I will compose it there and disclose if that proves wrong.

implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED for the composer (DoD 2/3/4). Suite red for exactly the intended reason: `Error: Cannot find module './expansion-admission.js'`, 1 failed | 41 passed, 1047 tests still passing, so the baseline is intact and the red is mine.

THE ALL-OR-NONE TEST MEASURES THE RESERVATION, NOT THE RETURN VALUE. `carries no preparation/identity/reservation/rows` passes against an implementation that strands a held budget reservation, so it is paired with a second assertion that compares the RESTORED meter buckets against the untouched view (`available: 1000, reserved: 0`). Skipping cancelReservation reddens that one and only that one. This is drill (d) pre-armed.

ORDERING IS WHAT MAKES THE PROPERTY REACHABLE AT ALL. Budget is reserved BEFORE the resource acquisition, so a late resource failure is the one path where a partial hold can exist. Every pure check (evidence, lineage limits, graph, fairness, bypass) runs before either reservation; a test asserts a refusal before any reservation reports `budgetReservationCancelled:false` so the two paths stay distinguishable.

CHILD WIDTH IS DERIVED, NOT SUPPLIED. The request's `lineage` accepts exactly `expansionDepth` and `nodesAddedInExpansion` — structural facts a receipt cannot see. A caller supplying `childWidth` is refused as a malformed request; the width fed to the limit check comes from the derived evidence. Test: "derives childWidth rather than accepting one the caller supplies".

DELEGATED CODE **AND** LAYER ARE ASSERTED SEPARATELY FROM ORIGIN. Five delegation tests pin (code, origin) and, where the surface has its own layer, the layer verbatim: EXPANSION_SCOPE_OVERLAP/SCOPE/EVIDENCE, ADMISSION_INPUT_MALFORMED/GRAPH, FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_UNDECLARED_RESOURCE/RESOURCE/FAIRNESS, BUDGET_RESERVATION_STALE_VERSION/BUDGET, AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT/RESOURCE. `origin` exists because the fairness layer vocabulary and my surface names collide on "RESOURCE" — without it, "which layer refused" is ambiguous exactly where two layers can both refuse.

TWO LOCAL CODES ARE MINTED AND EACH TEST SAYS WHY IN PLACE. rotateOnce returns ok:true with an IDLE disposition and reserveAll returns ok:true with outcome WAITING — both are NON-refusals that are nonetheless not admissions, and neither closed code tuple can express that. Everything else delegates.

N/N+1 AT ALL THREE LIMITS: depth 3 admits / 4 refuses ADMISSION_EXPANSION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, nodes 9/10 ADMISSION_EXPANSION_FANOUT_EXCEEDED, width 6/7 ADMISSION_EXPANSION_CHILD_WIDTH_EXCEEDED from a generated `wideReceipt(n)`. The codes are the LANDED admission ones because the limits are composed via checkExpansionLineage — no local 3/6/9 is declared, so admission-records.ts needs no export and I touch no unowned file. Drill (e) will mutate EXPANSION_LIMITS in its own file.

IDENTITY: 15 named perturbations, each asserted to change the identity, plus a set-cardinality test requiring all 16 identities DISTINCT (a per-case "differs from base" sweep passes even if two perturbations collide with each other). A separate test asserts the sweep generated a non-zero case count. Fields covered: revision, goalVersion, graphEpoch, observedAtSequence, sourceDigests, childKeys, expansionDepth, nodesAddedInExpansion, quality/dependency records, capacity snapshot, fairness opportunity, cap revision, proven bypasses, budget reservation, resource reservation. Presence of each bound key is checked by NAME rather than by snapshot — a snapshot re-baselines a dropped field instead of catching it.

DISCLOSURE: the test imports `../admission/admission-fixtures.js`, the package's own DEVELOPMENT_ONLY admission fixtures, the same precedent as admission-pass.test.ts and admission-invariants.test.ts. It is same-package, test-only, and no production file imports it; DoD 5's required grep over packages/scheduler/src/expansion for @moe/testkit|DEVELOPMENT_ONLY|@moe/runner is still empty. implementationPlan.description:
GREEN part 2: packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-admission.ts plus its LF `.js` bridge. The all-or-none composer.

ORDER MATTERS FOR ALL-OR-NONE: acquire nothing until every pure check has passed, or unwind precisely on failure. The safest shape is to evaluate all pure evidence and limit checks FIRST, then take reservations, so a late refusal cannot strand a held budget or resource. If you must reserve before a later check, the failure path must cancel every reservation taken — budget-reservation.ts exports cancelReservation:231 for exactly that, so compose it rather than leaving a reservation dangling.

Compose EXPANSION_LIMITS from admission-records.ts; do not redeclare 3/6/9.

Delegated refusals pass through VERBATIM with their own code and layer (DoD 3). Only mint an expansion-local code for a failure the composed surfaces cannot express, and say which in a comment.

THIS IS A PURE KERNEL (taskRail 3): it creates NO child run, lease, effect, slot, allocation activation or graph mutation. Reservation is not activation — `activateReservation` exists and must NOT be called here. Scope also excludes policy evaluation, approval, child activation, persistence and daemon composition, and forbids importing @moe/runner.

Below 400 lines; split if the composition and the identity construction crowd each other.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN part 2. `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` -> 42 files / 1120 tests, 0 failed. Baseline before my diff was 41 / 1047, so +1 test file and +73 tests, and the composer half contributed 42 of them (1078 after step 3).

I DID NOT REDECLARE 3/6/9, AND I ALSO DID NOT EXPORT THE CONST. Step 1 pre-authorised adding `export` to the module-private EXPANSION_LIMITS in admission-records.ts, which is not an owned path. That turned out to be unnecessary: `checkExpansionLineage` (admission-pass.ts:192) already ENFORCES the limits and returns the landed ADMISSION_EXPANSION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED / _CHILD_WIDTH_EXCEEDED / _FANOUT_EXCEEDED codes, so composing the checker instead of the constant gets the limits, the enforcement and verbatim delegated codes at once — and touches no unowned file. Drill (e) will mutate the numbers in their own file to prove the composition is real.

CHILD WIDTH IS DERIVED; DEPTH AND NODE COUNT ARE NOT, AND THE SPLIT IS PRINCIPLED. The request's lineage record accepts exactly `expansionDepth` and `nodesAddedInExpansion` — structural facts about the surrounding graph that a proposal receipt cannot see, so a caller is their only possible source. The width is PROVEN by the receipt, so a caller-supplied one would be a verdict; `childWidth` is absent from LINEAGE_KEYS and supplying it is refused as a malformed request.

ORDER IS THE ALL-OR-NONE MECHANISM, not a comment about it. Every pure check (evidence, lineage limits, admitGraph, rotateOnce, capacity re-derivation, cap revision, bypass claim) runs inside `pureChecks` before anything is reserved, so those refusals cannot strand a hold — there is none yet. Budget reserves before resources, which makes exactly ONE partial-hold path reachable, and that path calls cancelReservation and returns the restored buckets. `activateReservation` is NOT called; no child run, lease, effect, provider slot, allocation activation or graph mutation is created.

THE NEVER-STARTED PROOF IS A FACT, NOT A CLAIM. cancelReservation refuses without a neverStartedProofRef. This kernel creates no attempt, run, lease or effect, so nothing it reserved can have started; the ref is derived from the admission ref. A cancellation that nevertheless fails is disclosed as an extra BUDGET issue with budgetReservationCancelled:false, rather than reported as an unwind that happened.

CAPACITY IS RE-DERIVED THROUGH THE PRODUCTION VALIDATOR. rotateOnce has already accepted the capacity records, so running validateResourceCapacity again always succeeds today. It is there so the SNAPSHOT is derived rather than read off the caller's numbers, and so the failure stays closed if the two surfaces ever disagree.

THREE LOCAL CODES, EACH FOR A FACT NO CLOSED TUPLE CAN EXPRESS: REQUEST_MALFORMED (the envelope is mine; no surface sees it), NO_FAIRNESS_OPPORTUNITY (rotateOnce returns ok:true carrying IDLE — a non-refusal that is not an admission), RESOURCES_UNAVAILABLE (reserveAll returns ok:true carrying WAITING — same shape). Everything else delegates code and, where the surface has one, layer verbatim; `origin` is recorded beside the layer because fairness already owns a RESOURCE layer and so does the acquisition surface, so the delegated layer alone is ambiguous exactly where two layers can both refuse.

FILE SIZES, hand-measured with `grep -c ''`: expansion-admission.ts 309, expansion-preparation.ts 208, expansion-evidence.ts 218, expansion-receipt.ts 209. All under the 400 split bar. expansion-admission.ts is above the 250 soft target and I am disclosing that rather than splitting again: the four refusal adapters are shared by the pure checks and the reservation ordering, so hoisting the pure checks into a fourth module pushes the shared module to ~253 instead — the same overage in a different file plus one more file beyond the plan's owned paths.

THREE TS CASTS AT THE reserveForAdmission CALL are a signature accommodation, not an assumption: the reservation kernel re-parses each argument through isView/readRecord/readGate and refuses with BUDGET_RESERVATION_MALFORMED or _GATE_MALFORMED before touching a bucket. No `any` anywhere.

implementationPlan.description:
Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test; record the failing assertion. (a) Accept a caller-declared scope or capacity verdict instead of the derived one — the caller-positive test must redden; this is the defect the task exists to prevent. (b) Treat UNKNOWN evidence as a pass — the UNKNOWN test must redden. (c) Re-wrap a delegated refusal in a local code — the verbatim-delegation assertion must redden, proving the tests pin WHICH layer refused. (d) Leave a budget reservation held on a late capacity failure — the zero-partial-child assertion must redden; if it stays green your all-or-none test is only checking the return value. (e) Redeclare the limits as 4/7/10 locally — an N+1 boundary test must redden, proving the limits are genuinely composed. (f) Drop one field from the identity binding — the corresponding perturbation test must redden, proving every bound field actually participates.

All five owned files are NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is blind to them — hash with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff, and re-run the suite after each restore.
